fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responding units can identify it quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse without backing the full length of the access drive.
• Trim dense vegetation along the sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation that directly contacts or overhangs the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the perimeter of both structures.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of vegetation and obstructions so responders can move between the two structures quickly.
• Mark the location of the detached structure on any address or access information posted at the driveway entrance so arriving units know a second structure exists on the property.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can reach both structures without delay.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders have a clear sightline and travel path between the two buildings.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the foundation and walls.
• Clear dead leaves, pine needles, and debris from the roof and gutters regularly.
• Thin scattered trees close to the structure so their branches do not touch or overlap each other.
• Cut back shrubs along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway to a height that allows emergency vehicles to pass underneath.
• Remove or cut back vegetation growing in the center strip of the driveway to keep the travel surface clear.
• Create visible open ground between the shrubs and trees nearest to the structure so there is a clear gap with no continuous plant cover connecting them to the house.
• Keep the driveway edges mowed or cleared so vegetation does not narrow the usable width over time.
• Remove dead wood, dry grass, and accumulated debris from beneath the tree clusters near the structure.
• Thin shrubs scattered across the property closest to the structure, prioritizing those on the uphill or prevailing wind side.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the main road
